conclusion.justification: The report concludes that CoQ10 has not been reliably shown to relieve statin-associated muscle discomfort and is not an evidence-based routine treatment, while noting conflicting studies and that the evidence is limited rather than definitive proof of zero effect. This cautiously unfavorable view corresponds to leans_reject.
conclusion.label: leans_reject

report:
**Conclusion:** Your answer is broadly supported: CoQ10 has **not been shown reliably to relieve statin-associated muscle discomfort**, so it is not an evidence-based routine treatment.

**Why:**  
- In a randomized, placebo-controlled trial restricted to people with *confirmed* statin myalgia, CoQ10 did **not** reduce muscle pain (and pain severity was slightly higher than with placebo). This is especially informative because many muscle symptoms attributed to statins have other causes. [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4298455/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4298455/)  
- A 2020 systematic review/meta-analysis of seven placebo-controlled randomized trials found that the pooled analysis **did not favor CoQ10** for statin-associated myalgia. However, the trials were small and substantially heterogeneous, so the evidence is limited rather than definitive proof of zero effect. [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021915020301386](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021915020301386/)  
- There is conflicting literature: a 2018 meta-analysis reported improvement in pain, weakness, cramps, and tiredness. [https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/full/10.1161/JAHA.118.009835](https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/full/10.1161/JAHA.118.009835/) This disagreement likely reflects small, varied studies and differing symptom definitions.  
- The European Atherosclerosis Society consensus concluded evidence was insufficient to justify CoQ10 for statin myalgia. [https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article/36/17/1012/2465952](https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article/36/17/1012/2465952)

Do not stop a statin because of pain without discussing it with the prescriber; evaluation for other causes and adjustment of the statin regimen are generally more evidence-based approaches.
